Platform Builder 10.6.3 is a patch with a few fixes:

Built in game variables (like lives) or custom game variables can now be set in the title screen Startup command prompt and they won't be reset when you start a new game.
A small update was made with the introduction timeline in the example file.
Fixed: There is sometimes a problem getting the proper numbers on the right side of a formula in the command prompt.
Fixed: If you try to do a ground pound during a propel or homing attack, the character will be stuck.
Fixed: Backpack and cape is still visible if you left it active when you upload a character sprite sheet.
Fixed: Volume control in the music import screen is missing unless you import an introduction.
Fixed: Ground-pounding a custom block gives an error.

notes.title: Platform Builder 10.5.2
notes.notes:
Platform Builder 10.5.2 has a number of fixes. Most importantly, a system has been added to help restore missing games automatically. Some have reported this problem, and so here I am at 1 a.m. with my fingers crossed that this will fix the problem.

I suspect this issue originated with the Steam Cloud feature that was never meant to be activated for Platform Builder. I don't know how it switched on because nothing was configured properly, but I turned it back off.

10.5.2
-Added a function to help restore missing game files automatically.
-Built-in star items now use the levitate setting.
-Added a volume control for imported music (technically, we already had it, but it was not visible for a while).
-Fixed: The manager button appears when defeat settings for custom enemies is set to "Do: Nothing."
-Fixed: The assistant is not visible when speaking in Game Setup.
-Fixed: Right-clicking on edit button in the workstation doesn't work if the button is disabled.
-Fixed: The "select" button in enemy settings does not work for when the enemy defeat settings is set to "New Area". 
-Fixed: The wood tile set displays the wrong text in the workstation when it is selected.
-Fixed: The wrong message appears when you are asked to start a new project in simple or advanced mode.
-Fixed: Delay physic setting for custom projectile does not save correctly.

notes.title: New Demo and GIVEAWAY for Platform Builder!
notes.notes:
Finally, you can try before you buy! We just released a free demo for Platform Builder, which you can find on our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/885030/Platform_Builder/]game's store page[/url].

Here's the exciting part: Because of our need for feedback, [b]we are offering FREE KEYS to any of our new users of Platform Builder who check out our demo, fill out our survey, and join our Discord channel![/b] This offer is available for the first 150 respondents until December 1, 2023. It's rare for us to give away keys like this, so take advantage of this opportunity! First-time users of Platform Builder will receive more instructions on how to take the survey once they launch the demo.

The Platform Builder Demo gives you near-full control of every feature for building and playing a single sandbox level, as well as the opportunity to view and play an example file of a full game (made by yours truly).

—TingThing

notes.title: Updated EULA for Platform Builder
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Platform Builder's EULA on the Steam page has been updated. Here are the differences:

A new section has been added which says this:

"By using Platform Builder, you acknowledge that Platform Builder may collect and send quantitative data to the developer about how often Platform Builder is played on your computer, how long, and how it is used. This data is solely for the purpose of analytics, and none of the data is personal."

In other words, Platform Builder will collect some analytics as you play it. Steam already does this somewhat with all of their games, as do most websites out there.

Other than the new section, I also included the EULA for using the Explore Section in the main EULA, and a few things have been reworded for clarity. 

By continuing to use Platform Builder, you agree to the new EULA. You can view it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/eula/885030_eula_1]here[/url].

Best,
TingThing

notes.title: Platform Builder Reverted to 10.4.4
notes.notes:
Hey everyone,

I had to revert Platform Builder down one patch number from 10.4.5 to 10.4.4. The reason is that 10.4.5 was compiled with the latest version of Game Maker Studio, and I hadn't realized that the latest update changed how assets are stored in memory. This creates many fatal issues in 10.4.5, and I will need some time to update the code and re-stabilize Platform Builder.

Thanks for your patience and understanding!
TingThing

notes.title: Platform Builder's Category Switch
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

Platform Builder started as a simple "game-making game." But as I have continued to develop Platform Builder, so many new features have been added that it's starting to feel more like software. Users can now use a simple form of code (the command prompt), and those with the DLC can import their assets and export their games to .exe files.

Although the easy controls, colorful user interface, and casual nature of Platform Builder still have a "game" feel to it. [u]That's not going away.[/u] However, Platform Builder's capabilities have, in my mind, pushed it to the level of software. Because of this, I contacted Steam and asked them to switch us over. They approved, and the changes are in effect immediately.

Ultimately my hope is that those who are looking to create their own 2D run-and-jump Platformer games will find Platform Builder and recognize its incredible potential!

Thank you to those who have suggested I make the switch. ːsteamthumbsupː

notes.title: Platform Builder's Pricing Model is Changing
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Over the years, I have spent countless hours developing Platform Builder as a labor of love. A lot has happened with each new upgrade. When I released the first version of Platform Builder, there was no 2-player mode, no sprite designer, no explore section or .exe publishing, no commands or command prompts, no timelines or custom menus or custom sprites.

Things have really changed over the years, and now my business partner and I believe Platform Builder is ready to enter the market as a paid program. If all goes according to plan, Platform Builder Standard will become $14.99 on Friday, September 16th.

[b]If you already have Platform Builder in your Steam library, don't worry. You will continue to have full access to Platform Builder and all the free updates as it has always been for you.[/b] In fact, this change will benefit many of you! With Platform Builder becoming a paid program, we want it to feel more like a paid program. After the switch, Platform Builder Standard will allow custom physics and will remove all limits for custom items, enemies, etc. All that will be left for Platform Builder Pro is the ability to import your own game assets and export your games to .exe files. Consequently, Platform Builder Pro has gone down to only $4.99, effective immediately.

We believe this change will be healthy for the future of Platform Builder and increase its image to the public. Even with this new pricing model, we are confident that incoming players will get way more than they pay for. Thank you so much for being a part of this!

notes.title: Platform Builder 10 Beta
notes.notes:
Hello everyone!

If you haven't already noticed, [b]Platform Builder 10 Beta is available NOW[/b] for anyone interested to try it out! As always, there are a ton of new features, but this update is also the release of revamped graphics! You can see all of the changes on our [url=https://theplatformbuilder.com/forums/index.php?topic=2068.0]forum page[/url].

[i]How do I access Platform Builder 10 Beta?[/i]

It's pretty easy. From your steam library, look to the left with all of your games. Right-click on Platform Builder, select "Properties," and then under "betas," you'll see an option to use Platform Builder 10 Beta. This will cause Platform Builder to update so that the beta will launch next time you start.

Since this is a beta, be mindful that sometimes there are issues, but you can report any bug or errors you find [url=https://theplatformbuilder.com/report-bug-error/]here[/url]. Also, once you start working with Platform Builder 10, you cannot go back to those same game files with version 9. Because of this, you will be prompted to save a backup of all your files before you begin Platform Builder 10. This will also help in case something funky happens with your files while you work with a Beta version. ;)

It's been fun making these new features! I hope you enjoy it as much as I have enjoyed the process of coding this thing into life!

Cheers,
Ting_Thing

notes.title: Platform Builder 8 is Released!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! This is TingThing, the Dev. of Platform Builder,

Platform Builder 8 has arrived!

There are a LOT of new features that you can see [url=https://theplatformbuilder.com/forums/index.php?topic=1563.0]here[/url] and [url=https://theplatformbuilder.com/forums/index.php?topic=1591.0]here[/url], but one of the most important additions that I want to highlights is [b]the ability to export your games into a stand-alone .exe package with Platform Builder Pro[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33007942/9963f77af2fba5996652dd5a8af360e0f7156311.png[/img]
This is something I have wanted to do for a long time, and I finally figured out a way to do it! If you have supported this program by purchasing Pro, you will be able to export your games to run on their own directly through Platform Builder so you can share them with your friends or even upload to other indie game websites.

[h2]With all the great new features that are out, I believe this community could create a great selection of fun and creative games with Platform Builder![/h2]

Enjoy all of these new features,
TingThing
